releases.body:
Eight-episode debut season features Mission Wealth advisors offering financial planning perspectives and explores the intersection of financial strategy and human psychology.

SANTA BARBARA, Calif., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mission Wealth, a nationally recognized RIA, today announced the launch of its new podcast, Mission Wealth | With Purpose. The first season explores how Mission Wealth advisors guide individuals and families as they prepare for retirement, navigate inheritances and approach other significant financial decisions.

Real stories from wealth advisors about how people navigate pivotal life transitions, both personally and financially.

Hosted by Partner and Managing Director Jenna Rogers, the podcast brings together advisors from across the country for conversations grounded in real-life situations and personal experiences.

"Financial decisions often come at important turning points in people's lives, and knowing where to start isn't always easy," said Rogers. "Our goal is to make these conversations more approachable, helping listeners understand their options and the questions worth asking before making a decision."

The first season will cover topics including:

  • Living with purpose: How financial planning can support personal values, family priorities and a meaningful life beyond investments.
  • Navigating retirement: How Medicare, Social Security, taxes and retirement income decisions work together.
  • Preparing an estate plan: Key considerations around trusts, beneficiaries, gifting and communicating financial wishes with family.
  • Managing company stock: How employees and executives can approach concentrated stock positions, equity compensation and tax considerations.
  • Planning charitable giving: Strategies for incorporating philanthropy, appreciated assets and donor-advised funds into a year-end financial plan.
  • Preparing for business transitions: Financial considerations for business owners approaching a sale, succession or other major transition.
  • Choosing a financial advisor: What individuals and families should consider when hiring or changing financial advisors.
  • Navigating an inheritance: How to approach inherited assets, tax considerations and new financial responsibilities.

"Two families can face the same financial question and arrive at different answers," said Matthew Adams, CEO of Mission Wealth. "Their priorities, responsibilities and plans for the future all matter. That's an important part of financial planning we want these conversations to convey."

The first episode of Mission Wealth | With Purpose, "Planning for a Rich Life" with Stephanie Bruno, is out now on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, YouTube and other major platforms.

About Mission Wealth

Mission Wealth is a nationally recognized RIA that oversees over $17.6 billion in client assets under management. Mission Wealth is known for its service model, driven by a world-class technology stack that offers financial planning, investment counsel, tax strategies, estate planning coordination, philanthropic advice, and asset protection solutions tailored to each client's needs. IDAHO FALLS, Idaho, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Des Hague, Global CEO of Potandon Produce and Rä Foods, author and business advisor, today announced the launch of Onwards! with Des Hague, a new podcast featuring candid conversations with influential business leaders, entrepreneurs, elite athletes and personalities who have built global enterprises, navigated extraordinary challenges and redefined success.

Built around the philosophy "Real Business. Real Lessons. No Filters.", Onwards! takes audiences behind the decisions, turning points and personal experiences that shape exceptional leaders. From building multibillion-dollar businesses to navigating corporate transformations and reinventing careers, the series delivers practical insights rarely shared in traditional business interviews.

The confirmed lineup of guests for upcoming episodes includes:

  • Tom Park, former President of Walt Disney Global Retail and former executive leader of Belkin, Kenmore, Craftsman and DieHard, discussing the strategies behind building multibillion-dollar global empires.
  • Mike Penella, global food and beverage executive and former President of Conagra Foodservice, Sara Lee Bakery and Michael Foods, exploring the complexities of managing multibillion-dollar consolidations.
  • John Rota, global marketing executive, discussing how to build products, brands and strategies that resonate with consumers around the world.
  • Mark Garth, transformational CFO with leadership experience at Darigold, Perdue Farms and Maytag, sharing the financial and leadership lessons behind successful corporate transformation.
  • Jim Keyes, former CEO of 7-Eleven and Blockbuster, examining the opportunities and challenges of managing iconic global powerhouses.
  • James D. White, former Chairman, President and CEO of Jamba Juice and former Chairman of the Board of The Honest Company, offering a unique perspective on staying relevant, leading with purpose and winning the right way.
  • Tre Lucas, sharing lessons from transitioning from corporate America to startups, entrepreneurship and beyond.

Additional global business leaders, athletes and influential personalities are expected to join the Onwards! lineup as the series expands.

"We've been developing this concept for some time, but timing is everything," said Hague. "The moment feels right to bring these conversations to a wider audience. Everyone has a story, and some of the most valuable lessons come from the challenges we face along the way. With Onwards!, we want to share those experiences openly and honestly. Real Business. Real Lessons. No Filters."

Drawing on decades of global executive leadership and his own experiences navigating adversity, Hague brings a distinctive perspective to conversations designed to inspire, challenge conventional thinking and deliver practical insights audiences can apply to their own lives.

Onwards! with Des Hague will be available across major podcast platforms.

Guest appearances, strategic partnerships and sponsorship opportunities are available. For inquiries, contact paul.onwards@gmail.com.

Des Hague is a global business executive, entrepreneur, author and advisor with decades of experience leading and transforming organizations across multiple industries. He currently serves as Global CEO of Potandon Produce and Rä Foods. Throughout his career, Hague has championed leadership, innovation, resilience and the pursuit of excellence.

releases.title: ASTHO's Public Health Review Morning Edition Podcast Earns Bronze Anthem Award
releases.body:
Award honors the podcast's role in delivering timely public health news and expert insights to public health professionals nationwide.

ALEXANDRIA, Va., Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO) podcast, Public Health Review Morning Edition, received a Bronze Anthem Award in the Public Health, Health category. The award recognizes the podcast's ability to provide public health professionals with timely news, expert perspectives, and practical lessons from across the country.

Public Health Review Morning Edition provides concise daily updates on important public health issues, including policy, funding, workforce development, emergency preparedness, infectious diseases and other emerging challenges. Since launching in 2021, the podcast has published more than 1,200 episodes and receives nearly 10,000 monthly listens.

"Clear, timely communication is essential to a strong public health system," says Joseph Kanter, MD, MPH, ASTHO CEO. "Public Health Review Morning Edition helps health professionals stay informed, hear directly from experts and understand how public health issues are unfolding across the country. We're proud to see this work recognized by the Anthem Awards."

The podcast has featured a wide range of prominent voices in public health, journalism and public health leadership, including former U.S. Surgeon General Jerome Adams; former CDC directors Mandy Cohen and Robert Redfield; Alabama Department of Public Health state health officer Scott Harris; Indiana Department of Health state health commissioner Lindsay Weaver; U.S. Public Health Service and Chief Parasitic Diseases Branch, CDC, Captain Paul Cantey; epidemiologist Katelyn Jetelina; former Wall Street Journal reporter Julie Wernau; and bestselling author Stephen Covey.

The Anthem Awards, launched by The Webby Awards, recognizes impactful work by organizations and individuals advancing social good around the world. Public Health Review Morning Edition was selected as a finalist for the sixth annual awards from more than 2,500 entries submitted globally.

The award marks another milestone for ASTHO's podcast, which in 2023 received a Bronze Anvil Award of Commendation from the Public Relations Society of America.

Produced in partnership with Grod Media, Public Health Review Morning Edition is available on major podcast platforms, including Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

Learn more and listen to episodes at newscast.astho.org.

ASTHO is the national nonprofit organization representing the public health agencies of the United States, the U.S. territories and freely associated states, and Washington, D.C., as well as the more than 100,000 public health professionals these agencies employ. ASTHO members, the chief health officials of these jurisdictions, are dedicated to formulating and influencing sound public health policy and to ensuring excellence in public health practice.

Spotify rollout will expand across half of United's fleet by next spring; airline is advancing inflight innovation as it expects to offer 219,000 seatback screens by the end of 2027 and complete fleetwide Starlink installation before the end of 2027

CHICAGO, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- United and Spotify today announced a first-of-its-kind way for travelers to enjoy their favorite Spotify content in the sky: streaming directly from their personal Spotify account on the seatback screen. Customers can scan a QR code to securely log in to access the full Spotify catalog, including over 100 million tracks, along with millions of podcasts, playlists, videos and albums directly from their screens*. Passengers can pick up their favorite content right where they left off and save new favorites to enjoy long after their flight.

United is the first airline to let customers access their own Spotify account directly from a seatback screen, creating a more personal and connected entertainment experience built around the content they love. Powered by Starlink Wi-Fi, the integration allows travelers to watch performance videos like To All the Boys I've Loved Before: Full Cast Graphic Adaptation by Jenny Han and On Purpose with Jay Shetty – streamed directly from their own Spotify account. Once logged in, customers can access their personalized recommendations, playlists and saved content, and discover new recommendations tailored specifically to their listening and viewing habits, delivering a seamless listening experience that moves with them wherever they travel.

"Our customers are used to streaming entertainment that's tailored to them, and that level of personalization shouldn't stop when they board one of our planes," said Andrew Nocella, Chief Commercial Officer at United Airlines. "Now, thanks to Starlink, they can watch and listen to their own Spotify content right on their seatback screen and pick up their favorites right where they left off. From video podcasts and live performances to music and audiobooks, our collaboration with Spotify gives customers more of what they love onboard and is helping us create an elevated experience for everyone who chooses to fly United." 

"Bringing personal Spotify accounts to United seatback screens is a major milestone, creating a new way to experience Spotify in flight," said Ian Geller, VP of Business Development at Spotify. "With a quick QR code scan, passengers can bring their personalized Spotify experience to the screen in front of them — their recommendations, saved library, and favorite songs, podcasts, audiobooks, and videos — and enjoy it all on a big screen at 35,000 feet."

United introduced an exclusive collection of Spotify content on its seatback screens in June 2025, including more than 450 hours of audiobooks, video podcasts and music playlists. Since then, more than 2.3 million customers have enjoyed more than 1.9 million hours of Spotify content onboard. This new functionality builds on that by giving customers access to their personal Spotify account – from their saved playlists to tailored recommendations and more – directly from the seatback screen. The launch of the Spotify app integration builds on United's continued investment in personalization and the inflight experience.

United continues to invest in the inflight entertainment experience, in addition to Spotify, the airline gives customers access to more than 2,500 hours of premium entertainment content including Apple TV, HBO Max, A24 and Peacock. 

United is also elevating the onboard experience with Starlink. Starlink Wi-Fi is now available on more than half of United's daily flights and enables MileagePlus® members to stream, work, shop and stay connected across multiple devices in the air. The airline expects to complete Starlink installations by the end of 2027, bringing a faster, more connected and increasingly personalized experience to more customers. In addition, United currently offers more than 181,000 seatback screens across its fleet – more than any other major U.S. airline and about 85% of its mainline fleet – and expects to have more than 219,000 screens, nearly its entire mainline fleet, by the end of 2027.

How It Works

Customers on eligible flights can open the Spotify app from the seatback screen and scan the displayed QR code with their phone's camera. If already logged in to Spotify on their phone, their account pairs seamlessly with the seatback screen through a single-click verification. If not, they can log in securely on their phone and their personal library will appear on the seatback screen, allowing them to:

  • Resume music, videos, audiobooks and playlists where they left off and control playback
  • Browse their library and personalized recommendations
  • Save new favorites to their library
  • Enjoy Spotify directly on the seatback screen, bringing them even more of the content they love
  • Optionally use their phone as a companion remote, allowing them to browse, select titles and adjust playback right from their seat without leaning forward to touch the screen

Customers may log out at any time during the flight and will be automatically logged out of their Spotify account at the end of the flight.

*Available content and features vary by Spotify plan and market.

About United

At United, Good Leads The Way. With U.S. hubs in Chicago, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, New York/Newark, San Francisco and Washington, D.C., United operates the most comprehensive global route network among North American carriers and is now the largest airline in the world as measured by available seat miles. For more about how to join the United team, please visit www.united.com/careers and more information about the company is at www.united.com. United Airlines Holdings, Inc., the parent company of United Airlines, Inc., is traded on the Nasdaq under the symbol "UAL"

releases.title: Flagship poetry podcast, The Slowdown launches new season with bestselling writer of poetry and prose Maggie Smith to host
releases.body:
SAINT PAUL, Minn., Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Public Media and the Poetry Foundation today announce the launch of season 7 of the celebrated poetry podcast, The Slowdown with award-winning poet and writer Maggie Smith hosting. Starting November 2, 2026, Smith will be back to share a selected poem and thoughtful reflection every weekday, offering listeners a daily opportunity to find connection and calm through poetry. Earlier seasons of the podcast were hosted by award-winning poet Major Jackson and former United States Poets Laureate Ada Limón and Tracy K. Smith. 

Maggie Smith is the award-winning, bestselling author of nine books of poetry and prose, including Good Bones and Dear Writer: Pep Talks & Practical Advice for the Creative Life. Her latest book, A Suit or a Suitcase, a new collection of poems on the sometimes-blurry distinction between mind and body, and how the self shifts and moves through time and space was published by Washington Square Press/Atria in March 2026. Smith's second picture book for children, is forthcoming from Simon & Schuster in 2028.

"I'm so excited to be back hosting another season of The Slowdown. I began as a listener and a fan of the show, grateful to start my workday mornings with a poem, grateful for the gift of a meaningful pause. And now it's my pleasure, as host, to create those moments. So much of the writing life is solitary, and so much of our daily life moves at a relentless pace. The Slowdown offers a sense of connection: together, we take a moment out of our days to listen, discover, and reflect. I hope you'll join us and listen wherever you get your podcasts." Smith said.

Smith has received a Creative Writing Fellowship from the National Endowment for the Arts, a Pushcart Prize, and numerous grants and awards from the Academy of American Poets, the Sustainable Arts Foundation, the Ohio Arts Council, and the Greater Columbus Arts Council. Her poems and essays have appeared in The New York Times, The New Yorker, The Paris Review, The Nation, The Atlantic and The Best American Poetry.

New episodes of The Slowdown are available every weekday on Apple Podcasts, Spotify and all other podcast platforms. Listeners can subscribe to the show's newsletter, and follow along for updates at SlowdownShow.org and at @SlowdownShow on Facebook and Instagram. 

Maggie Smith writes about craft in her bestselling Substack newsletter, For Dear Life. You can find her on social media @MaggieSmithPoet. 

The Slowdown is produced by American Public Media in partnership with the Poetry Foundation.

About American Public Media

American Public Media® (APM) is the national programming and distribution division of Minnesota Public Radio® and reaches over 15 million listeners weekly across 1,000 public radio stations. APM is one of the largest producers and distributors of public radio programming in the world, with a portfolio that includes BBC World Service, Marketplace®, and the leading classical music programs in the nation. American Public Media also offers a diverse array of podcasts featuring the best in food, culture, entertainment, business and investigative journalism. For more information on APM, visit americanpublicmedia.org.

The new professional development hub from Enrollify, by Element451, helps higher education professionals turn AI experiments into real results, with courses taught by the network's own hosts

RALEIGH, N.C., Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Enrollify, the largest podcast network dedicated to higher education, today announced the launch of Enrollify Futures, a home for campus professionals to develop tangible AI skills. Its first courses are led by the network's hosts, a mix of higher ed leaders and AI practitioners, and designed to turn early AI use into everyday practice. The network will also feature AI-focused shows centered on the courses, and the new Enrollify AI Job Board connects those skills to learners' next opportunities. Element451, an early sponsor that launched its own show on the network in 2021, acquired Enrollify in 2023 to deepen its investment in professional development for colleges and universities. Today the network features eight flagship shows, with three of them ranking in the top 5% of more than 3.8 million podcasts worldwide, according to Listen Notes.

AI is reshaping how students learn and how campuses run. According to EDUCAUSE, 94% of higher ed employees used AI for work in the past six months, yet training remains the resource they say they need most. A 2026 Digital Education Council survey found that 88% of students use AI in their learning, but only 29% believe their instructors are well equipped to guide them. With the technology changing every few months, closing that gap takes ongoing training from the people who are doing the work themselves.

That's what Enrollify Futures provides. Rather than teaching a single tool, it prepares higher ed professionals for the way AI is already changing their jobs. Courses focus on durable skills that outlast any one model, such as judging what AI produces, deciding what to delegate, and designing workflows where people and agents work together. Learners build skills that compound across their careers, and their institutions gain staff who can redesign work, not just speed it up.

Futures launches with three inaugural courses, each designed around the daily work of higher ed teams. Every instructor is an Enrollify podcast host, hand-picked for the work they do with AI, and every course ends with a working result.

  • Building Your First Higher Ed AI Agent, led by Brian Piper. Over four weeks, learners build a scheduled, multi-skill agent and learn a method they can reuse in any tool their institution approves. Learners who demo a working agent earn the Enrollify AI Agent Builder badge.
  • AI for Enrollment Management & Student Engagement, led by Dr. Allison Turcio and Rishab Malhotra. Over six weeks, enrollment teams redesign one stage of their funnel and decide what stays human, what AI assists, and what AI can own.   • State of AI 101, led by Dr. JC Bonilla. This self-paced quarterly briefing covers what has changed in AI and what works now, and it ends with a 90-day action plan. Learners can take it on its own, and it's included with both course tracks.

Piper, host of "AI for U," is the former director of content strategy at the University of Rochester. Turcio, host of "The Application," is dean of enrollment and marketing at Siena University. Malhotra, co-host of "Higher Ed Pulse," is the founder of AIDO and a former enrollment AVP. Bonilla, academy director and co-host of "Higher Intelligence," is the former COO and head of AI at Element451.

"Nearly every higher ed professional is already using AI. What they're missing is someone who has done the work showing them how to rebuild their job around it," said Bonilla. "That's what our instructors do on their shows every week. Now they're teaching it."

Futures also includes the new Enrollify AI Job Board, which helps institutions reach candidates ready to lead their AI efforts. Element451 customers will have free access to Enrollify Futures resources when the full program becomes available in 2027.

"Car Concepts with Ralph Gilles," a new weekly video podcast takes listeners inside "the chamber of creativity" with the designers, engineers, and leaders who shape the vehicles the world loves

AUBURN HILLS, Mich., Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

  • Each episode goes beyond the product to the people behind it and examines why designers draw, how ideas take shape, and what gets the creative juices flowing
  • Season one guests include automotive legend Bob Lutz, Gorden Wagener, Cristy Lee, Garrett Reed, and Stellantis design leaders Gilles Vidal, Scott Krugger and more

Today, Stellantis launches "Car Concepts with Ralph Gilles," a weekly video podcast hosted by Stellantis Chief Design Officer Ralph Gilles that explores where the passion for cars meets the passion for art. In each episode, Gilles sits down with designers, engineers, executives and creators to uncover the stories, processes and inspiration behind past, present and iconic vehicles.

"There's an incredible amount of passion in the automotive industry, and the best stories belong to the people behind the products," said Gilles, chief design officer, Stellantis. "This industry is full of talented designers, engineers, creators and unforgettable characters, and everyone has a story about how they got here, what shaped them and what keeps them going. I wanted to create the types of conversations you have when hanging with friends in the garage, talking about cars, creativity, life and the experiences that define us. While the cars bring us together, the people and their stories are what inspired this podcast."

Inside the Chamber of Creativity

"Car Concepts" is built for anyone who has ever stopped to admire a great-looking car and wondered how it came to be. Conversations trace design as a story, vehicle and process, from the first sketch to the production vehicle, and examine how the craft continues to evolve with new technology and tools.

The podcast speaks to a broad audience:

  • Car enthusiasts who want the stories behind the vehicles they love
  • Students and up-and-coming designers looking for insight from the leaders who have walked the path before them
  • Design enthusiasts beyond automotive who appreciate creativity, craftsmanship and human ingenuity
  • Business leaders across the automotive industry, from suppliers and partners to the brands that serve consumers, fueled by the passion for the vehicles that move us

Every episode is recorded in person inside Stellantis' historic Conner Avenue Assembly Plant in Detroit, with heritage and new vehicles providing the backdrop for each conversation.

A Host Who Has Shaped Car Culture From the Inside

Few voices in the global automotive community carry Ralph Gilles' perspective. A car enthusiast who discovered design, Gilles joined the company as a designer in 1992 and today leads global design for Stellantis' portfolio of 14 iconic vehicle brands as a member of the Stellantis leadership team.

Along the way, he has served as president and CEO of the Dodge brand, president and CEO of the SRT brand and motorsports, and head of design for North America.

He has lived within the legacies of the Stellantis brands and has been entrusted to shepherd them forward.

Gilles also lives the culture he designs for:

  • Competitor in the Targa Newfoundland Rally, the Car and Driver One Lap of America and the SRT Viper Cup Series
  • Judge at leading concours d'elegance events, including Pebble Beach, Amelia Island and the EyesOn Design car show
  • Recipient of the 2023 EyesOn Design Lifetime Achievement Award and the Automotive Hall of Fame Young Leadership & Excellence Award
  • Bachelor of Fine Arts in industrial design from the College for Creative Studies, where he serves on the board of trustees, and an MBA from Michigan State University

That experience gives Gilles access and insight few hosts can match, as well as an ability to draw out stories his guests rarely share.

Season One Guests

The first season of "Car Concepts with Ralph Gilles" features conversations with:

  • Scott Krugger, head of North America design, Stellantis
  • Cristy Lee, TV host, mechanic/builder, real estate developer
  • Bob Lutz, automotive industry executive (retired)
  • Garrett Reed, creator, American Muscle HD
  • Gilles Vidal, head of enlarged Europe design, Stellantis
  • Gorden Wagener, head of Mercedes design (retired)

Additional guests will be announced throughout the season.

Where to Watch and Listen

New episodes of "Car Concepts with Ralph Gilles" will be released every Thursday in 2026, beginning Oct. 29.

  • Audio: Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube, Spotify and Audible

releases.body:
White House Historical Association President Stewart McLaurin and President Gerald Ford's Official Photographer David Hume Kennerly Explore the Stories Behind Iconic White House Photography

WASHINGTON, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The White House Historical Association today released a new episode of The White House 1600 Sessions podcast. Stewart McLaurin, president of the Association, sits down with David Hume Kennerly, Pulitzer Prize-winning former White House photographer. The episode offers a remarkable inside look at life in the White House in the mid 1970s through firsthand accounts behind his photographs.

Kennerly's storied career as a Chief White House Photographer began at age 27, when President Gerald Ford invited him to photograph his presidency in the days following President Richard Nixon's resignation in August 1974. In the episode, Kennerly reflects on the character and warmth of President Gerald Ford and First Lady Betty Ford, the mutual trust they developed, and the candid, unexpected moments he witnessed. Kennerly also discusses the many historic moments he documented throughout his career following his role at the White House, including the first photo of five living presidents, taken at the dedication of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library in 1991.

"These thousands of compelling photographs offer a rare glimpse into the presidency, capturing defining public moments and personal interactions that broaden our understanding of the Executive Mansion as an office and a home, and the people whose lives and service have shaped our shared history," said McLaurin.

Kennerly's photographs captured not only pivotal events and traditions in presidential history, but also illuminated informal interactions less frequently seen by the public, including Queen Elizabeth II sharing a laugh with President Ford at the Bicentennial State Dinner and President Barack Obama spending a quiet moment with First Lady Michelle Obama in the freight elevator of the Washington Convention Center on the evening of his inauguration in January 2009. Another memorable photograph shows Mrs. Ford dancing on the Cabinet Room table the day before President Jimmy Carter's inauguration in January 1977, which Kennerly interpreted as a symbol of her feminist advocacy in a historically male domain. 

"There wasn't one day that I took working at the White House for granted or didn't go through those gates thinking, 'Oh, my gosh, I can't believe I'm here'," said Kennerly.

Prior to his career-defining role at the White House, Kennerly photographed major pop stars, the 1969 World Series, the Vietnam War, and the aftermath of Robert F. Kennedy's assassination at the Ambassador Hotel. Throughout his career, Kennerly has photographed 13 American presidents, significantly contributing to the public's understanding of presidential history.

Through his personal recollections in his new book, "In the Room: 60 Years on the Front Lines of History," Kennerly offers a rare and intimate perspective on the American presidency.

The White House 1600 Sessions podcast is available on Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

The full video of this podcast episode is also available on the White House Historical Association's YouTube channel here.

The White House 1600 Sessions

The White House Historical Association's President Stewart McLaurin is the host of The White House 1600 Sessions, the Association's official audio and video podcast devoted to exploring the history, cultural impact, untold stories, and personal accounts of America's most iconic residence and highest office.

About the White House Historical Association

Founded in 1961 by First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy, the White House Historical Association is the nonprofit, nonpartisan organization entrusted with preserving and sharing the history of the White House. Supported entirely by private philanthropy and the sale of educational books and products, the Association reaches millions of students, teachers, and lifelong learners through research and scholarship initiatives, public programming, and the authoritative titles published by its independent press. Throughout each presidency, the Association works with the Offices of the First Lady and the White House Curator to acquire and preserve historic objects for the White House Fine and Decorative Arts Collection. The Association also operates The People's House: A White House Experience, a free, immersive, educational museum in Washington, D.C., which welcomes hundreds of thousands of visitors annually. To learn more about the White House Historical Association, please visit WhiteHouseHistory.org.

TORONTO, Oct. 22, 2026 /CNW/ -- LumiQ, an audio-first continuing professional education (CPE) platform, today announced a partnership with the Florida Institute of CPAs (FICPA), giving Florida CPAs the ability to purchase curated podcast learning paths that count toward their required CPE. FICPA members can now purchase LumiQ's CPE podcast learning paths directly through the FICPA, with an initial set of 10 learning paths covering topics from auditing and taxation to business development and real-world business case studies.

The partnership makes the FICPA, which represents more than 20,000 members across Florida, the first state CPA society to offer its members this model of podcast-based CPE through LumiQ. It reflects the FICPA's ongoing effort to give Florida CPAs more flexible and engaging ways to meet their requirements.

Shelly Weir, President & CEO of the Florida Institute of CPAs, said, "The FICPA continues to search for solutions that both modernize CPE and uphold the standards of the profession. With podcasts having already reshaped the media and education landscape, our partnership with LumiQ will provide a new, engaging option for earning CPE that meets our members where they are."

Each CPE podcast learning path is a curated set of episodes built around a single topic. Members access their learning paths through LumiQ's platform or mobile app, allowing them to complete their CPE from anywhere and on their own schedule. The initial set of 10 includes Audit Nightmares, which examines real-world audit failures and the lessons behind them; Business Transformation in Practice, which explores how organizations like LEGO and Kodak navigated major turning points; and Tax Foundations: Individual, Estate, and Trust, which covers the basics of individual and estate tax planning. The full list of learning paths is available on LumiQ's website.

Joel Lessem, CEO of LumiQ, said, "We're excited to bring these podcast learning paths to FICPA's members. Each one lets CPAs dive deep on a single topic, from single audits to real-world business transformation case studies, so they walk away with practical knowledge that keeps them future-ready as the profession evolves."

FICPA members can purchase LumiQ's learning paths through FICPA.org.

LumiQ is an audio-first CPE platform for accounting and finance professionals that turns required learning into strategic upskilling. Its podcasts are developed to be enjoyed and retained, giving professionals the knowledge and confidence to grow their careers.

Hosted by Meridian President & CEO Jay-Ann Gilfoy, Season 3 moves beyond the traditional podcast format with in-studio video conversations designed to bring viewers closer to the entrepreneurs, advocates and community leaders shaping the future of small business.

"Behind every business is an ecosystem of people, advice, partnerships and community support that helps turn an idea into something sustainable. This season is about having honest conversations with some of the people who are helping create those conditions and sharing insights that small business owners can actually use."

The Small Business, Big Impact Podcast is designed for entrepreneurs, founders, gig workers and those building, growing or supporting small businesses, with conversations grounded in the real opportunities and challenges business owners face.

Season 3 brings together voices from across the small business ecosystem to explore the ideas and issues shaping entrepreneurship today, from financial confidence and workforce development to advocacy, leadership, community impact and inclusive economic growth.

"Small business owners are navigating a lot, and they need more than financing," said Gilfoy. "They need people who understand their ambitions, trusted advice, strong networks and partners who are invested in their success. That's the bigger conversation we want to have with Small Business Big Impact."

Season 3 launches on October 22 with new episodes following monthly through March 2027. For the first time, audiences will be able to watch full episodes on YouTube in addition to listening through major podcast platforms, including Apple, Spotify, and Amazon.

PEEKSKILL, N.Y., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What does it truly mean to age well? How can families prepare for changing care needs without sacrificing independence, dignity, or quality of life?

These questions drive the return of Embracing Angels, an educational podcast hosted by Robert Dalton, CEO of Angels on Call Homecare, an award-winning New York homecare organization specializing in Dementia, Parkinson's disease, and personalized aging-in-place services.

Real Conversations. Diverse Voices. Meaningful Perspectives.

Embracing Angels extends our belief that aging should never mean losing your identity, purpose, or voice. The conversations we start today can meaningfully shape the care people experience tomorrow."

releases.title: OutRival's "The New Normal" Podcast Goes Inside the AI Playbooks of the World's Largest Brands, Including Marriott Vacations Worldwide, Azamara Cruises, SNHU and More
releases.body:
The weekly show has published 13 episodes with the leaders of some of the largest organizations in higher education and travel, including Marriott Vacations Worldwide, Azamara Cruises, Southern New Hampshire University, Western Governors University, Miami Dade College and Dallas College, plus the U.S. Department of Labor. Thirty episodes are recorded, with 100 planned by 2027.

MIAMI, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The New Normal, the show about how enterprises are deploying AI agents and generating real ROI, today released its 13th episode and confirmed a weekly cadence through 2027. Presented by OutRival, the Miami-based company building AI digital workers for voice, SMS and email, the show has recorded 30 episodes with the leaders of some of the largest organizations in higher education, travel and government, and plans to have 100 recorded by 2027. New episodes publish every Thursday at thenewnormal.fm.

The New Normal is hosted by OutRival Co-Founder and CEO Ruben Harris and Co-Founder and President Timur Meyster. Vice President, Head of Travel Jeff Herzfeld, a 20-year cruise and hospitality sales operations veteran, co-hosts the travel episodes. The show's next chapter is insurance: recordings with carrier, agency and brokerage leaders begin Q4 2026, co-hosted by OutRival's Vice President, Head of Insurance, Eric Weinstein.

The Premise

Most AI coverage is about what might happen. The New Normal is about what already did. Every episode puts a senior operator in the chair to walk through the use cases they actually deployed, the numbers they actually saw, and the decisions they got wrong along the way. No vendor pitch, no futurism, just leaders who run large organizations explaining how the work is changing inside them.

How the Show Is Made

Every episode is recorded in person. The OutRival team gives each guest two options: fly to OutRival's headquarters in Miami, or the hosts fly to the guest's headquarters. The second option is the one the team prefers, because being on site is how you learn how a leader is actually thinking about these decisions, and it puts a light on the people behind the C-suite: the enrollment counselors, advisors, sales associates, contact center teams and technologists responsible for creating an amazing experience for every student, traveler and policyholder. The episodes are produced by Mike Landsberg and Thomas Risavy of Grove Station Studios.

The show was built for industries that live on the phone: higher education, insurance and travel, where the relationship between a brand and the people it serves runs through millions of calls, texts and emails. Nobody proves the point like Bob Becker, the cruise industry sales legend responsible for more than $50 billion in sales at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, who filled ships primarily through the phone.

His episode, released today, is live here. Those are the industries where getting AI right matters most, because a human will always be in the loop at some point to create a delightful experience for the student, the traveler or the policyholder. The leaders on the show have already made the hard calls about where that point is, and they are thinking past the first call: how AI agents can help their people provide care through the entire journey, from the first inquiry to the trip after this one. Together, the institutions represented in the first 13 episodes serve more than one million students a year and millions of travelers.

Why the Show Exists

Every new normal begins as the risk most people avoid today and the standard everyone copies tomorrow. After conversations with more than 300 enterprise leaders, the OutRival team found that most companies are still not running AI in production at scale, and the few that are have a lead the rest of the market cannot see coming. The New Normal exists to put those leaders on the record. The guests are the ones putting digital workers on the org chart, writing job descriptions for them, and reorganizing teams so humans and AI work side by side.

Most companies still treat AI as reactive support, a smarter way to answer the phone once a customer finally calls. The leaders on the show flipped it. They use it to reach out first: the inquiry that never got a callback, the application someone almost finished, the policy up for renewal, the guest ready to book the next trip. The show covers inbound and back-office use cases too, but the questions it keeps coming back to are about where leaders stopped waiting and started the conversation themselves.

13 Episodes, Three Industries, One Format

The show launched in June 2026 with higher education, added the U.S. Department of Labor as its first government guest, and opened its travel chapter in October. Published episodes, in order:

  1. Kermit Cook, CEO, Penn Foster: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/penn-foster-kermit-cook
  2. Madeline Pumariega, President, Miami Dade College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/miami-dade-college-president-madeline-pumariega-on-deploying-ai-at-scale-in-higher-education
  3. Scott Pulsipher, President, Western Governors University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/wgu-scott-pulsipher
  4. David Andrews, Chancellor, UMass Global: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umass-global-david-andrews
  5. Mark Milliron, President, National University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/national-university-mark-milliron
  6. Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/snhu-lisa-marsh-ryerson
  7. Gregory Fowler, President, University of Maryland Global Campus: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/umgc-gregory-fowler
  8. Taylor Stockton, Chief Innovation Officer, U.S. Department of Labor: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dol-taylor-stockton
  9. Raghu Krishnaiah, Chief Operating Officer, University of Phoenix: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/university-of-phoenix-raghu-krishnaiah
  10. Justin Lonon, Chancellor, Dallas College: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/dallas-college-justin-lonon
  11. Mike Flaskey, President and COO, Marriott Vacations Worldwide: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/marriott-vacations-worldwide-mike-flaskey
  12. Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO, Azamara Cruises: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/azamara-cruises-dondra-ritzenthaler
  13. Bob Becker, the King of Outbound, former sales executive at Carnival, Norwegian and Celebrity, released today: thenewnormal.fm/episodes/bob-becker-king-of-outbound

Insurance episodes, co-hosted by Eric Weinstein, will cover how carriers, agencies and brokers are putting AI agents to work. Additional higher education, travel and insurance executives are already recorded and scheduled.

What the Guests Are Saying

"I want more of our people to be able to do the heart work, and I want to offload the hand work," said Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President of Southern New Hampshire University, on where AI belongs at a university serving 300,000 learners.

"A pilot is an initiative. Scale is a transformation," said Madeline Pumariega, President of Miami Dade College, on why the college went all in rather than piloting.

"You don't have the reach that these digital workers do," said Mike Flaskey, President and COO of Marriott Vacations Worldwide, on what AI adds to a 1,400-person sales organization.

"So if AI's coming and it can help us, let's go," said Dondra Ritzenthaler, CEO of Azamara Cruises.

"Hope is a pretty poor strategy in business," said Bob Becker, the sales leader who built the outbound model used across the cruise industry, on why he started AI with one use case.

What the Hosts Are Saying

"The most useful conversations about AI were happening in private, between operators, and nobody was recording them," said Ruben Harris, Co-Founder and CEO of OutRival. "Thirteen episodes in, the pattern is clear. The leaders winning with AI did not wait for a perfect pilot. They put it to work on the conversations they were already having with students, travelers and policyholders, and they measured it. We have 30 of those stories recorded, and we will have 100 by 2027."

"Every enterprise is being told to deploy AI. Almost nobody is being shown what it looks like when it works," said Timur Meyster, Co-Founder and President of OutRival. "We built OutRival to put digital workers into production at scale, so we know the difference between a demo and a deployment. The New Normal exists to make that difference public. The leaders on this show are not forecasting. They are reporting results, and they are putting their names on them."

"I started on the phones at Carnival and spent twenty years running sales floors, so I know how this industry reacts to a pitch about the future. We've heard it. We've bought it. Most of it didn't work," said Jeff Herzfeld, Head of Travel at OutRival. "This show skips the pitch entirely. It's leaders in cruise, vacation ownership and hospitality telling you what they actually did with this technology and what happened next. Honest, specific, and on the record. That conversation used to happen behind closed doors. Now you're in the room."

Who Should Watch

The show is built for presidents, chancellors, provosts and enrollment leaders in higher education; CEOs, contact center and revenue leaders in cruise, vacation ownership and hospitality; carrier, agency and brokerage executives in insurance; and anyone responsible for deciding how AI shows up in front of a student, a traveler or a policyholder.

The show is also tailored towards established vendors and startups who are obsessed with learning how their customers and potential customers think. New episodes publish every Thursday, with short clips released across YouTube Shorts, Instagram and LinkedIn.

About OutRival

OutRival makes it possible for brands to genuinely care about every single person they serve. New Schools for New Orleans series examines demographic change, enrollment decline, and the future of public education

NEW ORLEANS, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Across the country, public school systems are confronting a new reality: fewer students, tighter budgets, and difficult decisions about how to sustain strong schools as enrollment declines.

A new podcast from New Schools for New Orleans (NSNO), "The Future Is Smaller: What New Orleans Learned Before America Had To," examines these challenges through the experience of a city already navigating them. Launching October 15, the series brings together education leaders, researchers, school operators, students, and families to explore how demographic shifts affect school finances and academic opportunities, and what communities can do to prepare for a smaller future.

The series also addresses a critical question facing school leaders and districts: how to protect and build upon academic progress while simultaneously reshaping school systems for a smaller student population.

The first episode, "The Last Miss Douglass," premieres October 15, with new episodes released monthly on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Amazon Music, and other platforms.

"The Future Is Smaller" is produced by Jenny Dubin and Laura Hawkins. Associate Producers are Jason Rhein and Taylor Jackson. Sound design is by George Ingmire, and production management is by Elephant Quilt Productions. The podcast is sponsored by New Schools for New Orleans, with special thanks to Dana Peterson and Tiffany Delcour.

Listen and subscribe: https://rss.com/podcasts/the-future-is-smaller/

A National Challenge New Orleans Is Already Navigating

The number of school-age children is declining in communities across the country, driven by falling birth rates, population shifts, migration, and other demographic changes. For school systems largely funded based on student enrollment, those shifts can have significant consequences. In New Orleans, those pressures are already visible.

Over the past five years, K–8 enrollment has declined approximately 9%, while ninth-grade enrollment in 2026 is approximately 11% lower than in 2022. Meanwhile, New Orleans recorded its fifth consecutive year of academic growth on Louisiana's state assessments in 2026, improving three percentage points in students achieving Mastery or above.

The podcast builds on NSNO's longstanding work to help New Orleans public schools plan for a more sustainable system. Since 2022, NSNO has published regular analyses of enrollment, school capacity, and financial trends, helping school leaders, policymakers, and the public understand how demographic shifts are affecting schools today and what they could mean for the future. Through research and advocacy, NSNO has encouraged long-term planning that protects strong schools and directs limited resources toward students and educators.

New Schools for New Orleans is a nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to excellent public education. For 20 years, the organization has supported New Orleans schools through investments in educators, research, advocacy, and school sustainability. Learn more at www.nsno.org.

New series brings together executives, technologists and innovators to explore where XR is today, where it's headed and what business leaders need to know

JAFFREY, N.H., Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shivoo Studios, an immersive media and XR production company, today announced Reality Reframe, a new podcast and video series exploring extended reality through candid conversations with the people building, implementing and experiencing the technology firsthand.

Hosted by Alison Dean, Reality Reframe is designed to make immersive technology understandable and useful to business leaders—without the hype or marketing speak.

Each conversation explores the questions leaders should be asking as immersive technology continues to evolve: What is it? Where is it going? What should organizations do next? And what should they avoid?

"There's a real gap between what people think XR is and what the technology is capable of today," said Sterling Youngman, CEO of Shivoo Studios. "Some people have never experienced it. Others may be judging it based on something they tried years ago—or an experience that simply wasn't very good. Reality Reframe is about learning from the past, understanding where we are today and looking at what's coming next by hearing from the people who have actually done the work—the good, the bad and everything in between."

Upcoming conversations will feature voices from across immersive technology, entertainment, interactive experiences and business, including Jon Snoddy, co-founder and CEO of Operative Games and former head of Research & Development, Technology and AI studios at Walt Disney Imagineering; Spencer Lindsay, founder of eTribe; Bob Chambers, co-CEO of The Producers Group; and Peiman Fallahian Sichani, XR creative technologist and co-founder of Agora XR.

Together, these guests bring perspectives spanning interactive storytelling, real-time 3D, themed entertainment, augmented and virtual reality, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Future episodes will feature both people who helped shape the field and those actively building and implementing what comes next.

"You shouldn't need to be an XR expert to understand why this technology matters," said Dean. "My job is to ask the questions a smart, curious business leader would want answered—and sometimes the questions they may not know to ask yet. If every conversation leaves someone seeing the possibilities, risks or decisions a little differently, we've done our job."

As immersive technologies move beyond experimentation into real-world applications, Reality Reframe will look beyond the success stories to examine what actually happened: what worked, what didn't, what changed along the way and what others can learn from the experience.

The series is also inviting people on both sides of the XR experience to join the conversation. Business leaders who have commissioned or implemented immersive projects—as well as the technologists, studios and creators who have built them—are encouraged to share their experiences, including projects that succeeded, projects that fell short and lessons learned along the way. Those interested in sharing their story or being considered for a future conversation can contact rrguest@shivoostudios.com.

The technology is changing. Reality Reframe asks whether it may also be time to change the way we look at it.

Reality Reframe will be available in audio and video formats on major podcast platforms and YouTube, with launch details and additional guests to be announced soon.

Reality Reframe is produced by Shivoo Studios.

New series will bring candid conversations about diagnosis, daily life, research, and the search for treatments beyond the gluten-free diet to a global audience

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Celiac disease has never had a platform — or a voice — quite like this.

The Celiac Disease Foundation has announced the launch of Inside Celiac, a new signature podcast hosted by acclaimed actress Katie Lowes, known to millions for her standout roles in Scandal, Inventing Anna, and The Hunting Wives. Drawing on her extraordinary ability to connect with audiences and her deeply personal experience living with celiac disease, Lowes will lead candid conversations that bring greater national attention to this serious, often-overlooked autoimmune condition.

Each episode of Inside Celiac will bring together leading medical and nutrition experts, patients, advocates, researchers, and other influential voices to explore what it truly means to live with celiac disease. Topics will include the often-long road to diagnosis, the everyday realities of maintaining a strict gluten-free diet, emotional health, family life, pediatric celiac disease, long-term medical care, groundbreaking research, clinical trials, and the urgent search for treatments beyond the diet.

"Living with celiac disease affects so much more than what is on your plate. It shapes how you travel, celebrate, work, parent, and move through the world," said Lowes. "I am thrilled to host Inside Celiac and create a space where people can hear honest stories, learn from trusted experts, and feel less alone. This series is about giving our community a stronger voice while helping the broader public understand the very real impact of this disease."

Celiac disease is a serious genetic autoimmune disorder in which ingestion of gluten causes damage to the small intestine and can lead to significant short-and long-term health consequences. Its symptoms can vary widely, contributing to delayed and missed diagnoses. While a strict gluten-free diet is currently the only treatment, maintaining the diet can be medically, socially, emotionally, and financially burdensome.

"Inside Celiac represents a significant new chapter in how we educate, engage, and advocate for the celiac disease community," said Marilyn G. Geller, chief executive officer of the Celiac Disease Foundation. "By pairing Katie's recognizable voice and powerful storytelling with the Foundation's trusted expertise and international reach, we have an extraordinary opportunity to elevate celiac disease in the public conversation. We want millions of people affected by this disease to feel seen and heard while building greater awareness of the urgent need for earlier diagnosis, better care, and treatments beyond the gluten-free diet."

The series will translate complex medical and scientific topics into accessible conversations while centering the lived experiences of patients and families. Planned episodes will explore the current state of celiac disease, the diagnostic journey, manifestations beyond the gastrointestinal system, pediatric care, gluten-free nutrition and labeling, follow-up care, mental health and quality of life, persistent symptoms, disease prediction and prevention, clinical trials, emerging therapies, and the future of celiac disease care.

"The science of celiac disease is advancing rapidly, but there remains a considerable gap between what researchers and clinicians are learning and what patients, families, and the wider public understand about the condition," said Dawn Adams, M.D., president of the Society for the Study of Celiac Disease. "Inside Celiac can help close that gap by bringing accurate, evidence-based information into engaging and relatable conversations."

Through Lowes' authentic and approachable hosting style, Inside Celiac will invite listeners into conversations that are informative, inspiring, and grounded in both scientific evidence and real-world experience. The podcast will also highlight the people driving progress across the celiac disease community, from researchers pursuing new diagnostics and therapies to advocates working to improve food safety, access to care, and quality of life.

Inside Celiac will premiere on Thursday October 15, 2026, with new episodes available on the third Thursday of each month. Listeners can find the series on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pandora, iHeart, YouTube, and all platforms where podcasts are hosted.

To learn more about Inside Celiac and receive updates when new episodes are released, visit www.celiac.org/insideceliac.

About the Celiac Disease Foundation

The Celiac Disease Foundation is the nation's leading patient advocacy organization for celiac disease. For more than three decades, the Foundation has worked to accelerate diagnosis, treatments, and a cure through research, education, and advocacy. The Foundation leads programs that connect patients with clinical trials, advance medical education, support patients and families, and elevate celiac disease as a public health priority. Learn more at celiac.org.

About Katie Lowes

Katie Lowes is an acclaimed actress, director, producer, and podcast host known for her roles in the television series Scandal, Inventing Anna, and The Hunting Wives, as well as numerous film, television, theater, and voice performances. Drawing on her own experience with celiac disease, Lowes is committed to using her platform and storytelling abilities to increase understanding of the condition and amplify the voices of patients and families.

releases.title: Bielat Santore & Company Releases Episode 7 of the Owner's Edge Podcast Series: "New Jersey Liquor Licenses Part 2: Reforms to Inactive Licenses"
releases.body:
ALLENHURST, N.J., Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Commercial real estate brokerage firm Bielat Santore & Company has released Episode 7 of its Owner's Edge Podcast Series. The episode provides restaurant operators, license holders, developers, lenders, and municipal officials with an authoritative breakdown of New Jersey's major liquor license statutory overhauls.

New Jersey recently reformed its retail alcoholic beverage licensing framework twice within less than three years. These legislative updates ended the long-standing practice of indefinite dormancy for inactive "pocket" licenses, established structured activation timelines, and opened new intermunicipal transfer mechanisms designed to drive economic redevelopment.

Key Highlights Covered in Episode 7 (Part 2):

  • Ending Indefinite 12.39 Relief (P.L. 2023, c.290): Historically under N.J.S.A. 33:1-12.39, inactive Class C license holders could repeatedly petition the Director of the Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) for good-cause "12.39 relief" to maintain dormant licenses across consecutive terms.
  • The 2026 Reset & Revised Quartile Timetable (P.L. 2026, c.46): Enacted on July 23, 2026, P.L. 2026, c.46 superseded key portions of the 2024 law, resetting the four-group inactive license quartile schedule to run one, two, three, and four years from July 23, 2026.
  • Municipal Extensions & 30-Day ABC Appeals: Under the 2026 law, municipal issuing authorities possess expanded discretion to grant extensions beyond two consecutive inactive terms when a licensee demonstrates documented good-faith efforts to activate or transfer the license.
  • Three Distinct Intermunicipal Transfer Pathways: P.L. 2026, c.46 replaced the earlier contiguous municipality restrictions with three flexible transfer procedures to serve qualifying redevelopment, revitalization, or improvement areas[6]:
  1. Municipal Sale of a Newly Authorized License: Allows a municipality authorized to issue a new license to offer it at public sale to private bidders or to the highest bidding municipality statewide[14][15].
  2. Owner-Initiated Transfer: Permits an inactive license holder or contract purchaser to transfer a license to a qualifying redevelopment premises located in the same county or a contiguous municipality in an adjoining county[14][16].
  3. Receiving Municipality RFP: Enables a population-capped receiving municipality to solicit statewide RFPs to acquire an inactive license from the lowest qualified bidding owner for a designated redevelopment project[14].
  • Impact on License Asset Value & Market Strategy: While the 2026 reforms expand market potential across municipal and county borders, asset valuation now heavily relies on documented marketing history, active project pipelines, municipal alignment, and strict adherence to statutory deadlines rather than passive scarcity.

About Bielat Santore & Company

Bielat Santore & Company is a New Jersey commercial real estate brokerage specializing in restaurants, hospitality properties, business enterprises, and liquor licenses. For more than 45 years, the firm has advised hospitality operators, buyers, developers, lenders, and municipalities on the acquisition, sale, valuation, and regulatory transfer of commercial assets throughout New Jersey.

releases.body:
NEW YORK, Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Conversations around suicide and mental health are often brushed off in our culture, leaving many with feelings of isolation and helplessness and fears around being judged. The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP) addresses this head-on, launching a new season of its podcast channel where mental health experts and those with their own personal experiences related to mental health and suicide have honest, authentic, and open conversations, sharing insights from real people and communities, as well as the field's latest scientific developments and research.

Officially launched in December 2025, the AFSP Podcast Channel is entering its second season. In new episodes of Ask Dr. Jill, Strong Talk, and Elevating Voices, listeners can expect to learn about the latest research in the field, hear from changemakers who are reshaping mental healthcare, and have their real mental health and suicide-related questions answered by researchers, advocates, and licensed mental health professionals.

Season two's kickoff episodes in October:

  • Ask Dr. Jill, "What Can We Do to Prevent Physician Suicide?": Host Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman and Corey Feist, co-founder & CEO of the Dr. Lorna Breen Foundation, discuss the problem of physician suicide: the causes, the impact, and what we can do to prevent it
  • Strong Talk, next episode airing Oct. 21: Host Vic Armstrong has a candid conversation with Gemma Correll, bestselling author and graphic novelist (Anxietyland), known for integrating humor into their story of living with and navigating anxiety and depression

What's in store this season:

  • Dr. Lynnette A. Averill, a researcher specializing in psychedelics and their potential applications in mental health, on what research says about mental health and the use of psychedelics
  • Megan McCoy, CFT™, LMFT, and PhD, on the connection between personal finances and mental health – and how people can manage their emotions related to financial stress
  • Faye Seidler, LGBTQ+ suicide prevention advocate, on trans and LGBTQ+ suicide prevention and access to care in local communities
  • Vikram Patel, co-director of Harvard's Mental Health for All Lab, on what must be done to provide mental healthcare support care in low-resource settings
  • Dr. Ellie Foster, the co-director of Education for the Kevin Love Fund, on the role public figures and athletes play in empowering youth to explore vulnerability and have honest mental health conversations
  • Cultural considerations of mental health and suicide prevention in diverse communities

"We will be having conversations that combine real world experiences and research findings and offer our audience actionable content," said Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman, the host of Ask Dr. Jill and AFSP senior vice president of Research. "The new season invites listeners to meet and learn from interesting people who are changing the way we access mental health resources, making them more accessible to all," said Vic Armstrong, the host of Strong Talk and Elevating Voices and AFSP VP for Health Equity and Engagement.

The AFSP Podcast Channel houses the following shows:

Strong Talk is hosted by Vic Armstrong, AFSP's vice president for Health Equity and Engagement. Each episode features conversations with experts, advocates, and changemakers about how they're reshaping mental healthcare to make it accessible to all. The show covers topical issues that affect the mental health of various communities.

Elevating Voices is a roundtable discussion series where we bring together leaders from diverse communities to understand the unique mental health experiences they face and explore the ways we can all help to support and amplify progress.

Ask Dr. Jill features Dr. Jill Harkavy-Friedman, AFSP's senior vice president of Research, answering urgent and real mental health questions with the latest scientific research and conversations with fellow experts in the field.

Visit afsp.org/podcasts to learn more.

The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention is dedicated to saving lives and bringing hope to those affected by suicide, including those who have experienced a loss. AFSP creates a culture that's smart about mental health through public education and community programs, develops suicide prevention through research and advocacy, and provides support for those affected by suicide. Led by CEO Robert Gebbia and headquartered in New York, with its Policy and Advocacy Office in Washington, D.C., AFSP has local chapters in all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico, with programs and events nationwide. Learn more about AFSP in its latest Annual Report and join the conversation on suicide prevention by following AFSP on Facebook, X, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and TikTok.

The American Foundation for Suicide Prevention and The Jed Foundation (JED) intend to merge as equals to form AFSP/JED, the nation's largest nonprofit dedicated to preventing suicide across the lifespan, and bringing hope to those affected by suicide loss or risk. The AFSP/JED mission would reflect a commitment to bring together AFSP's research, advocacy, chapter network, and loss-support expertise with JED's comprehensive approach to suicide prevention and evidence-informed youth mental health programs, creating greater scale, reach, and impact at a time of urgent national need. Read more about our recent announcement.

The news follows the show's national 2026 Best of the Year Award in Tech & Media, from a program created by former Hearst Magazines senior editors.

The Signal Awards are "mission-focused on uplifting the podcast medium by recognizing the most potent, meaningful and unprecedented audio projects being made today." Its judges – ranging from author Jay Shetty to content executives at Ted Talks, NPR and YouTube -- are described as "the architects, instigators and trailblazers of the medium."

The finalist episode, "Writing to Surprise Ourselves: Fire Survivor Kathleen Katims' Saved by a Story," is also in the running for the Signal Listener's Choice Award, a global public vote that drew more than 385,000 votes in 2025. Fans can vote through Oct. 15 at vote.signalaward.com. Gold, Silver and Bronze winners will be announced Oct. 20.

The recognition is remarkable given how the show began. Two weeks after the January 2025 "fire hurricane" devastated two Los Angeles communities, veteran podcast host Kim Marshall -- who escaped the Palisades Fire on foot with a small suitcase and two dogs -- launched #L.A. Rising with no network behind it, just a $5,000 small business grant from L.A. County Supervisor Lindsay Horvath's office and a pro bono production partner. Her goal: a trusted place for survivors' stories of resilience, and for expert resources and wellness tools, long after national media moved on.

"What stood out most to me was the raw authenticity: a survivor host sharing survivor stories, without the distance much disaster coverage carries," said one Best of the Year judge.

With Emmy-winning broadcaster Giselle Fernandez as Advising Producer, #L.A. Rising has expanded to disasters worldwide, from flooding in Brazil and Texas Hill Country to Category 5 Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica. Its premise: lessons learned from one disaster can be a catalyst of hope and inspiration for the next. Wellness Lift segments pair each story with coping strategies like deep breathing, contrast bathing, meditation and understanding grief.

International podcast agency NOVA helps produce the show. "This wasn't just a local story — it was a global moment," said NOVA CEO Hayden Lyon. "When Kim came to us with #L.A. Rising, launching it pro bono was an easy decision."

Since early 2026, Marshall and NOVA also help produce After the Fire USA's "How to Disaster" podcast on megafire recovery.

The subtitle says it plainly: "Human expertise structured for AI agents." Each episode is an on-the-record conversation between two named, verifiable human experts. Not a script read by a voice clone. Not content generated by a model. Ringmaster designs each conversation so that answer engines can find the expertise inside it, pull it apart, and cite it back to the people asking questions.

AI-generated podcasts already exist. They recycle what machines already know. Cited Conversations captures what they don't: original expert perspective from a conversation that hasn't happened yet.

Each episode is built using Ringmaster's Plan, Capture, Transform (PCT) Framework™. The PCT Framework™ designs questions around AI visibility gaps before the recording begins, captures structured expert dialogue, and transforms each conversation into a library of content assets that answer engines can index and cite. Today, a single 45-minute expert conversation already produces as many as 40 content assets for human audiences. Cited Conversations is the start of building AI-specific assets on top of that same conversation.

"We've spent eight years helping companies connect with their customers through expert conversations. Now we're helping them connect with the machines that talk to their customers," said Casey Cheshire, Founder of Ringmaster. "A great podcast used to mean somebody listened all the way through. Now it also means an AI agent can find the ninety seconds that matter and hand it to someone who never pressed play."

The launch is timed to International Podcast Day, September 30. More than 4.7 million podcasts have been created worldwide (Podcast Index, 2026). The number built for an AI audience: one.

"This is just the beginning. The number of shows designed for AI consumption will surpass the ones that aren't," Cheshire said. "And the 4.7 million podcasts that already exist will rethink how they serve both audiences. The content is already there. It's just trapped in audio."

The podcast is available for AI agents at citedconversations.com. (The audio is there for curious humans.)

Ringmaster will unveil the show live at the Connect to Market community event, a private roundtable for B2B marketing leaders, on September 30 at 3:00 p.m. ET. The session is themed "Creating Content for Humans and AI," where Cheshire delivers a lightning talk introducing Cited Conversations.

releases.body:
NOVATO, Calif., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Brayton Purcell LLP is highlighting a recent episode of Bloomberg's Big Take podcast, "Crafting America's Favorite Countertops Is Killing Workers," that brings national attention to the growing artificial stone silicosis crisis affecting artificial stone countertop fabrication workers across the United States.

The episode examines the fatal health risks associated with fabricating artificial stone countertops, a product that has become one of the nation's most popular countertop materials. Through the story of former countertop fabricator Tyler Jordan, Bloomberg explores the devastating impact of artificial stone silicosis, the litigation filed by affected artificial stone fabrication workers, and the ongoing debate regarding responsibility within the industry.

Artificial stone is at least 90% respirable crystalline silica, and the remaining approximately 10% consists of highly toxic dyes, resins, glues, and heavy metals. During fabrication activities such as cutting, grinding, polishing, and shaping slabs, enormous quantities of nano-sized, high-surface area toxic artificial stone dust is released into the air.

When inhaled, these particles penetrate deep into the lungs and become embedded in lung tissue. The resulting inflammation and scarring leads to artificial stone silicosis, a devastating, progressive, incurable, and fatal disease. Unlike many occupational diseases, artificial stone silicosis continues to progress long after exposure has ended.

According to Bloomberg labor reporter Josh Eidelson, artificial stone contains significantly higher levels of crystalline silica than natural stone products. During the podcast, he noted that artificial stone can contain approximately 93% crystalline silica, compared with substantially lower amounts in materials such as marble.

The Bloomberg episode focuses heavily on the experience of Tyler Jordan, who began working in his family's countertop fabrication business after graduating from high school. As artificial stone became an increasingly large part of the shop's work, he spent much of his time fabricating artificial stone slabs.

Jordan recalled that he was told artificial stone was stronger, less porous, and more resistant to staining than natural stone. However, according to the podcast, he and other workers were not warned that artificial stone presented significantly different health risks.

While still in his twenties, Jordan began experiencing severe health problems, including unexplained weight loss, chest pain, back pain, and other symptoms. Following extensive medical testing and a lung biopsy, he was diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis.

The consequences extended beyond lung disease. Jordan later developed autoimmune disease and kidney failure and ultimately received a kidney transplant from his father. His illness forced him to leave the industry and relocate his family.

His story reflects a troubling trend documented by physicians and researchers around the world. While silicosis has existed for centuries, countertop workers who fabricate artificial stone are increasingly being diagnosed at younger ages and experience more severe and rapidly progressing disease than has historically been associated with silica exposure.

Bloomberg reported that thousands of cases of artificial stone silicosis have been identified worldwide. In the United States, workers in their twenties, thirties, and forties have been diagnosed with artificial stone silicosis, raising concerns among physicians, researchers, and public health professionals.

The podcast also examines litigation brought by workers who allege that exposure to silica released during artificial stone fabrication caused artificial stone silicosis and other serious illnesses. Approximately 700 workers throughout the United States have filed lawsuits against companies involved in manufacturing and distribution of artificial stone slabs. Workers allege that artificial stone is an extraordinarily hazardous product, and that the risks associated with artificial stone fabrication were not adequately disclosed. Defendants have denied wrongdoing and continue to maintain that artificial stone can be fabricated safely.

At the same time, policymakers continue to debate how best to respond to the growing crisis. Proposed responses discussed during the podcast range from restrictions on artificial stone fabrication to legislation that would affect certain claims involving manufacturers.

"Bloomberg's reporting highlights the profound impact artificial stone silicosis can have on workers and their families. Many of the individuals being diagnosed are experiencing debilitating lung disease and serious complications at an age when they should be building careers and raising families. As awareness of this occupational disease continues to grow, it is important for affected workers to understand their legal rights and the options that may be available to them," said James Nevin, Partner at Brayton Purcell LLP.

The Bloomberg episode emphasizes that artificial stone silicosis affects far more than a worker's lungs. Careers are cut short, families face financial hardship, and workers confront serious medical complications that affect multiple organ systems and lead to premature death.

To listen to the podcast, visit the Big Take Spotify page.

NEW YORK, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FOX News Podcasts will broaden its original podcast slate with FOX News' the Girls, a new personality-driven conversation series featuring an array of leading female voices. The announcement was made today by FOX News Digital and New Media President Porter Berry and Megan Albano, Executive Vice President of Morning Programming & Program Development. "the Girls" will debut on October 1st, with new episodes dropping every Thursday across all podcast platforms, including FOX News Digital, YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Podcasts.

Each episode of FOX News' the Girls will include a rotating cast of co-hosts week to week, moving beyond the traditional news roundtable for a free-flowing conversation that can go anywhere — politics and pop culture; money and marriage; parenting, relationships, careers, or the group chat-worthy story of the day. Nothing is off the table. Showcasing multiple distinct perspectives, the conversation will revolve naturally around the issues impacting real life with undeniable chemistry, refreshing candor and no script. The first episode will feature FOX News Media stars Rachel Campos-Duffy, Harris Faulkner and Kat Timpf, newly named FOX News contributor Melissa DeRosa and former ESPN host Samantha Ponder.

In commenting on the announcement, Berry said, "the Girls is a natural addition to our growing podcast portfolio, and we're thrilled to continue expanding our slate of distinctive shows that complement our existing lineup while creating new opportunities for our audience to engage with our content."

Albano added, "We're excited to deliver a no-holds-barred format that captures the authenticity and perspectives of the many dynamic women of FOX News Media and beyond."

Bringing together unique female voices and experiences spanning news, politics, sports, comedy and culture, the premiere episode will feature a variety of viewpoints and backgrounds:

  • Rachel Campos-Duffy joined FNC in 2016 and currently co-hosts FOX & Friends Weekend. A mother of nine, she is a New York Times bestselling author and previously appeared on MTV's The Real World.
  • Emmy Award-winning journalist Harris Faulkner has been with FNC since 2005 and anchors The Faulkner Focus and co-hosts Outnumbered. She is also a New York Times bestselling author and mother of two daughters.
  • Kat Timpf, who joined FNC in 2015, is a panelist on Gutfeld!, comedian and two-time New York Times bestselling author. A mother and breast cancer survivor, she has spoken candidly about motherhood, loss, and her cancer diagnosis.
  • Veteran democratic strategist Melissa DeRosa previously held several senior roles in former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo's administration, becoming the first woman to serve as secretary to the governor.
  • Samantha Ponder is a former host of ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown and a mother of three children.

The new podcast is the latest addition to FOX News Media's new media division which features an established suite of podcasts including Hang Out with Sean Hannity, Ruthless, Will Cain Country, Planet Tyrus and The Riley Gaines Show.
